title: Study Tutor Map
name: Study Tutor
lede: Every concept you’ll build, the file it lives in, and the tool that does the work, all linked. Pick anything to see what it touches.
footer: Drawn from PLAN.md as of 5 October 2026. Study material: Dive into Deep Learning by Zhang, Lipton, Li and Smola, CC BY-SA 4.0.

items.name: Tooling: uv, ruff and pytest
items.why: One command builds the same environment on your laptop and on CI.
items.you: Ran `uv sync`, `uv run pytest` and the ruff checks.
items.claude: `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version` and the smoke test.

items.name: Git, GitHub and your first pull request
items.why: History, branches and pull requests are how changes reach main safely.
items.you: Ran the git commands, created the repo and opened the pull request.
items.claude: The docs and `.gitignore`.

items.name: CI and the rule that protects main
items.why: Every pull request is checked on a fresh machine before it can merge.
items.you: Added the rule on main.
items.claude: `.github/workflows/ci.yml`.

items.name: Your Groq key and the book PDF
items.why: The two inputs M1 needs.
items.you: Created `.env` and downloaded the PDF into `data/`.
items.claude: `.env.example`.

milestones.title: One question, graded, with the passage shown

items.name: A rough first version in one file
items.why: See the whole tutor work in your first session. Every later concept replaces one rough piece with a real one.
items.you: The loop: show the question, read your answer with `input()`, print the grade.
items.claude: The two Groq calls, with their prompts written inline. It runs with `uv run --with openai --env-file .env scratch/first_loop.py`, so nothing is added to the project.

items.name: Turning the PDF into prose with page numbers
items.why: Only clean prose should ever reach retrieval and the LLM.
items.you: `classify_block()`: label each text block as prose, code, math, caption or header, using the fonts found in chapter 1.
items.claude: PDF reading, a listing of chapter 1’s fonts and sizes, bookmarks to topics, the topics table, the ingest command, tests.

items.name: Chunking
items.why: Questions come from passages of 120–350 words that never cross a topic.
items.you: `chunk_paragraphs()`, including what to do with a very short topic or a very long paragraph.
items.claude: Joining paragraphs split across pages, the passages table, tests.

items.name: Embeddings and vector search
items.why: Find passages by meaning when you type a topic.
items.you: `search(query, k, topic=None)`. Tiny example first: cosine similarity in NumPy.
items.claude: Model loading, embeddings with the section title in front, the Chroma index and its rebuild, the distance cut-off, the retrieval check.

items.name: Structured output (question writing)
items.why: The LLM answers in an exact shape, and code checks every quote it gives.
items.you: The question-writing prompt and the `QuestionSet` schema.
items.claude: The LLM wrapper, the quote check, the question pool, the token log, 429 handling.

items.name: Grading grounded in the passage
items.why: Grades come only from the passage, and the same answer always gets the same grade.
items.you: The grading prompt, the `Grade` schema, and five test answers with the grade each should get.
items.claude: The same-answer check, the attempts table, the “no support found” path, `scripts/regrade.py`.

items.name: The study loop: state, nodes, edges
items.why: Turns separate functions into one loop that runs step by step.
items.you: The state and the `build_graph()` wiring.
items.claude: Node functions that call concepts 1–5.

items.name: Conditional edges
items.why: Plain code decides the next step, so routing costs no tokens.
items.you: The routing function: ask, write again (once), or skip the passage.
items.claude: Retry counters, tests.

items.name: Pausing for your answer
items.why: The loop has to wait for you across separate web requests.
items.you: The node that calls `interrupt()`, and resuming.
items.claude: The in-memory checkpointer, session ids, a command-line driver.

items.name: API and UI
items.why: Study in the browser instead of the terminal.
items.claude: FastAPI routes and the Gradio page.

milestones.title: Ask the book, your first agent

items.name: Tool calling
items.why: Lets the LLM ask your code to run something, here a search of the book.
items.you: The `search_book(query)` tool definition: the description and parameters the LLM reads.
items.claude: Tool calls in the LLM wrapper, running a requested search, tests with a fake LLM.

items.name: The agent loop as a graph
items.why: The one place where the LLM chooses the next step, with code capping it.
items.you: The routing function: search again, answer, or stop after 3 searches.
items.claude: The agent subgraph (an LLM node and a tool node) and its message history.

items.name: Answers grounded in several passages
items.why: Classic RAG: answer from several retrieved passages, with every citation checked.
items.you: The answer prompt and the `BookAnswer` schema.
items.claude: The quote check on every citation, the “no support found” path, the Ask the book box, the asks table.

items.name: Hybrid search
items.why: Keyword search catches exact terms that meaning search can miss.
items.you: Reciprocal rank fusion: merging the keyword ranking with the embedding ranking.
items.claude: Keyword search with SQLite FTS5, the hybrid `search_book`, a comparison on the retrieval check.

milestones.title: Your feedback, the grading report, multiple choice

items.name: Capturing your feedback
items.why: Your corrections feed scheduling and the same-answer check.
items.claude: “Grade is wrong” with a grade picker, “Flag” with 4 reasons, the marks and flags tables.

items.name: Measuring the grader
items.why: An honest number for how good the grader is.
items.you: The agreement calculation on sampled grades, and a table of the tutor’s grade vs. yours.
items.claude: An agree or disagree question on every 4th grade, and the report page.

items.name: Multiple-choice questions
items.why: Quicker reviews, graded in code with zero LLM calls.
items.you: The MC prompt and schema.
items.claude: Grading MC in code, an MC pool per passage, the typed/MC/mixed choice, the options UI.

items.name: Growing the regression set
items.why: Catches a grader-prompt change that makes grading worse.
items.you: About 10 more answers, picked from grades you disagreed with, and the grade each should get.
items.claude: Adding them to the set `scripts/regrade.py` runs.

items.name: Adding chapters 2–10
items.why: More material, one checked chapter at a time. Before chapter 11, flag counts decide whether to switch to the book’s Markdown files.
items.you: Run the ingest command for each chapter.
items.claude: The Markdown reader, only if the PDF text proves too messy.

items.name: Scheduling with FSRS
items.why: Each passage comes back just before you would forget it.
items.you: The update function: final grade → FSRS rating → the passage’s updated card.
items.claude: Card storage, the review log, a card created the first time a passage is studied.

items.name: Due reviews first
items.why: Reviews take priority over new material.
items.claude: Most overdue first in “You choose”, the next unused question per review, a “reviews due” count.

items.name: Tagging mistakes
items.why: Knowing how you were wrong, not just that you were.
items.you: Extend the `Grade` schema and grading prompt with a mistake type and the wrong statements.
items.claude: The mistakes table.

items.name: Spotting mix-ups with retrieval
items.why: Catches answers like “you described classification, not tagging”.
items.you: `find_confused_topic()`: the closest other topic to a wrong statement.
items.claude: Storing the topic pair.

items.name: Pattern and weak-topic rules
items.why: Turns one-off mistakes into things worth following up.
items.you: The pattern rule: the same mix-up or mistake type twice in your last 10 answers.
items.claude: The weak-topic rule, and resolving a pattern after correct follow-ups.

items.name: Routing to follow-ups
items.why: The loop goes after your mix-ups on its own.
items.you: The routing function after grading: follow-up or normal next question.
items.claude: The follow-up node, and “You choose” adding follow-ups and weak topics.

items.name: Resuming after a restart
items.why: Stop mid-question and pick up exactly there later.
items.you: Switching the checkpointer to SQLite, and the resume logic.
items.claude: The sessions table, the “Resume” button, `checkpoints.db`.

items.name: Progress view
items.why: See where you stand at a glance.
items.claude: Topics studied, reviews due today and this week, weak topics, active mix-ups.

items.name: Demo mode
items.why: Strangers can try it without using up your free quota.
items.you: The per-visitor limit check.
items.claude: A throwaway database per visitor, a daily cap on LLM calls, a demo banner.

items.name: Packaging and hosting
items.why: A live link that works in any browser.
items.claude: The Dockerfile, the Hugging Face Space, the Groq key as a Space secret, a build that loads every checked chapter.

items.name: Demo video (backup)
items.why: Something to show if the live demo is down.
items.you: Recording a 3-minute walkthrough.
items.claude: The script of what to show.

tools.name: PyMuPDF
tools.what: Reads the PDF: its text, fonts, page numbers, and the bookmarks that become topics.
tools.note: It’s AGPL-3.0, which is why the whole repo is AGPL-3.0.

tools.name: bge-small-en-v1.5
tools.what: Turns text into a vector of 384 numbers, so passages can be found by meaning. Runs on your CPU, for free.
tools.note: Each passage is embedded with its section title in front; short queries get bge’s search prefix.

tools.name: Chroma
tools.what: Stores the passage vectors and returns the ones closest to a query.
tools.note: A derived index: it can always be rebuilt from SQLite. Uses cosine distance.

tools.name: SQLite FTS5
tools.what: Keyword search (BM25 ranking) built into SQLite, for hybrid search in Ask the book.

tools.name: Groq
tools.what: The LLM. gpt-oss-20b writes questions, gpt-oss-120b grades typed answers, and from M2 an agent answers Ask the book.
tools.note: Free tier, per model: 30 requests/min, 1K requests/day, 8K tokens/min, 200K tokens/day.

tools.name: openai SDK
tools.what: The Python library that sends every LLM call. Groq speaks the same API, so switching provider only means editing `.env`.
tools.note: Every call goes through `llm.py`; no LangChain chat models.

tools.name: Pydantic
tools.what: Defines the exact shape of every LLM answer (`QuestionSet`, `Grade`, `BookAnswer`) and reads your settings from `.env`.

tools.name: LangGraph
tools.what: Runs the study loop as a graph of steps and pauses it while it waits for you (`interrupt` plus a checkpointer). From M2 it also runs the agent loop.

tools.name: SQLite
tools.what: The source of truth: topics, passages, questions, your answers, grades, marks and the review schedule.

tools.name: fsrs
tools.what: The spaced-repetition scheduler: decides when each passage comes back, from your final grade.
tools.note: Learning steps are turned off, so a passage never comes back in the same session.

tools.name: FastAPI
tools.what: The web server. Passes the page’s clicks on to the study loop.

tools.name: Gradio
tools.what: The screen you study on, mounted inside FastAPI.

tools.name: uv
tools.what: Installs the exact package versions in `uv.lock`, on your laptop and on CI.

tools.name: ruff
tools.what: Checks and formats the code. CI fails a pull request when it complains.

tools.name: pytest
tools.what: Runs the tests for the predictable parts of the code. Tests never call the real LLM.

tools.name: Git + GitHub
tools.what: History, branches and pull requests. A concept reaches main only through a pull request whose checks pass.

tools.name: GitHub Actions
tools.what: CI: runs ruff and pytest on a fresh machine for every pull request.

tools.name: Docker
tools.what: Packages the app so the Hugging Face Space can run it. Installed before M7, so the image can be tested locally.

tools.name: Hugging Face Spaces
tools.what: Free hosting for the public demo.

tools.name: OBS Studio
tools.what: Records the backup demo video.

flow.title: A study turn
flow.hint: What happens, in order, each time the tutor quizzes you. Pick a step.

steps.label: Load a chapter
steps.text: Once per chapter, before any studying: read the PDF, keep only prose, group it into topics from the bookmarks, cut passages, save them and embed them. No LLM runs here, so it uses none of the free quota.

steps.label: Pick a passage
steps.text: A typed topic finds the closest passages by meaning, or says “the material doesn’t cover this”. “You choose” takes due reviews first (M4), then mix-up follow-ups and weak topics (M5), then the next new passage.

steps.label: Get a question
steps.text: The next unused question from the passage’s pool of 3. An empty pool means one LLM call writes 3 more, and code checks that each quote is really in the passage.

steps.label: Wait for your answer
steps.text: The graph pauses with `interrupt()`, and its state is saved until your answer arrives in a new web request.

steps.label: Grade it
steps.text: An answer seen before reuses its grade. A typed answer is graded by the LLM against the passage; multiple choice is checked in code (M3). From M5 the mistake gets tagged.

steps.label: Show grade and passage
steps.text: The grade, what’s missing or wrong, and the passage it was based on, with its page and section number.

steps.label: Next, Stop, or ask
steps.text: A second pause. Meanwhile you can mark the grade wrong or flag the question (M3), or ask the book a question (M2): an agent searches up to 3 times and answers with checked citations.

steps.label: Save and schedule
steps.text: Your final grade is saved, and FSRS decides when this passage comes back (M4). Next goes back to step 1; Stop lets you resume later (M6).
